```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("BurmeisterGetz_2025_iptacopan_healthy"))$reference`
* Article: [Clin Pharmacol Ther 2025;117(5):1358-1368](https://doi.org/10.1002/cpt.3559)
  (open access; [PMC11993288](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11993288/)).
  The Supplementary Appendix (Data S1) holds the derivation of the binding model.

Iptacopan is an oral inhibitor of complement factor B, a soluble, hepatically
produced plasma protein (about 150 ug/mL) that iptacopan binds with nanomolar
affinity. Because factor B is abundant but saturable at the clinical dose,
iptacopan shows small-molecule target-mediated drug disposition: its unbound
fraction falls as total concentration falls. In the phase I hepatic-impairment
study CLNP023A2105 every plasma sample was assayed for both total and unbound
iptacopan, and Burmeister Getz et al. fitted a **two-site competitive
equilibrium binding model** to the paired concentrations:

$$
C_{tot} = C_u + \frac{f_{B,avail} \cdot C_u}{K_D + C_u} + C_u \cdot \frac{1 - f_{u,max}}{f_{u,max}}
$$

(unbound drug, drug bound to factor B, drug bound non-specifically to the
other plasma proteins; Figure 2a). The model has no time dependence. The
packaged form takes total iptacopan as a time-varying covariate and returns
the unbound concentration from the single meaningful root of that quadratic
(main-text equation; Supplementary Appendix eq. 2),

$$
C_u = f_{u,max}\frac{b}{2} + \sqrt{\frac{f_{u,max}^2}{4} b^2 + f_{u,max} C_{tot} K_D},
\qquad b = C_{tot} - \frac{K_D}{f_{u,max}} - f_{B,avail},
$$

together with the fractional occupancy of available factor B,
`occ = Cu / (KD + Cu)` (Supplementary Appendix eq. 3).

The authors fitted the model **separately to each hepatic-function group**,
so the library carries four models with the same structure and
group-specific parameters:

```{r models}
models <- c(
  "Healthy controls" = "BurmeisterGetz_2025_iptacopan_healthy",
  "Mild HI" = "BurmeisterGetz_2025_iptacopan_mild_hepatic",
  "Moderate HI" = "BurmeisterGetz_2025_iptacopan_moderate_hepatic",
  "Severe HI" = "BurmeisterGetz_2025_iptacopan_severe_hepatic"
)
group_levels <- names(models)
mw_iptacopan <- 422.52 # g/mol, Table 3 footnote b

pars <- lapply(models, function(m) {
  th <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(m))$theta
  c(bmax = exp(th[["lbmax"]]), kd = exp(th[["lkd"]]), fumax = th[["fumax"]])
})
par_tab <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(pars, as.list), .id = "group")
knitr::kable(par_tab, digits = c(0, 2, 2, 2))
```

# Population

`r sum(sapply(models, function(m) rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(m))$population$n_subjects))`
adults received a single fasted oral 200 mg dose of iptacopan at a single
site: 16 healthy controls, 8 with mild (Child-Pugh A, score 5-6), 8 with
moderate (Child-Pugh B, 7-9) and 6 with severe (Child-Pugh C, 10-15) hepatic
impairment (HI). Each HI participant was matched to a healthy control by sex,
age (+/- 10 years), body weight (+/- 15%) and smoking status. Median age was
59.5 years (31-75), median weight 86.8 kg (59.5-116.0), 47.4% were female and
94.7% White (Table 1). Serum albumin fell from a median 44.5 g/L in controls to
30.5 g/L in severe HI, and bilirubin rose from 6.8 to 50.5 umol/L. Total and
unbound iptacopan were measured at 22 post-dose times from 15 min to 240 h.

Each model's `population` metadata carries its own group's demographics:

```{r population}
pop_tab <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(models, function(m) {
  p <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(m))$population
  data.frame(
    N = p$n_subjects,
    `Age, median (range)` = paste0(p$age_median, " (", p$age_range, ")"),
    `Weight range` = p$weight_range,
    `Female (%)` = p$sex_female_pct,
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}), .id = "Group")
knitr::kable(pop_tab)
```

# Source trace

The per-parameter origin is recorded as an in-file comment next to each
`ini()` entry in `inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/BurmeisterGetz_2025_iptacopan_*.R`.

| Equation / parameter | Healthy | Mild HI | Moderate HI | Severe HI | Source location |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lbmax` (fB,avail, nM) | log(1874.30) | log(1775.56) | log(1403.16) | log(880.36) | Table 3, row 'fB,avail, nM (ug/mL)' |
| `lkd` (KD, nM) | log(9.63) | log(10.89) | log(8.00) | log(8.84) | Table 3, row 'KD, nM' |
| `fumax` | 0.25 | 0.32 | 0.34 | 0.49 | Table 3, row 'fu,max' |
| `propSd` | fixed(0) | fixed(0) | fixed(0) | fixed(0) | Supplementary Appendix 'Statistical analyses' (proportional error; magnitude not reported) |
| Molecular weight 422.52 g/mol | | | | | Table 3 footnote b |
| Binding equation (total from unbound) | | | | | Figure 2a; Supplementary Appendix eq. 1 |
| Closed-form unbound concentration | | | | | Main-text equation after Figure 3; Supplementary Appendix eq. 2 |
| Factor B occupancy `Cu / (KD + Cu)` | | | | | Main text 'Target occupancy throughout the dosing interval'; Supplementary Appendix eq. 3 |

# Simulation

Because the model is algebraic, a "simulation" evaluates it on a grid of total
concentrations. Each grid point is an observation record; `time` is a dummy
index.

```{r simulate}
ctot_grid <- exp(seq(log(5), log(2e4), length.out = 200))

solve_group <- function(model_name, ctot) {
  ev <- data.frame(
    id = 1L,
    time = seq_along(ctot) - 1,
    evid = 0L,
    amt = 0,
    CP_IPTACOPAN_NGML = ctot
  )
  rxode2::rxSolve(readModelDb(model_name), events = ev, keep = "CP_IPTACOPAN_NGML") |>
    as.data.frame()
}

sim <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(models, solve_group, ctot = ctot_grid),
  .id = "group"
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    group = factor(group, levels = group_levels),
    ctot_nm = CP_IPTACOPAN_NGML * 1000 / mw_iptacopan,
    cu_nm = Cu * 1000 / mw_iptacopan
  )
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 2b -- binding components in healthy controls

Total iptacopan against unbound iptacopan (both nM) for the healthy-control
parameters, split into the three binding states of Figure 2a.

```{r figure-2b, fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 4.5}
p_h <- pars[["Healthy controls"]]
fig2 <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(group == "Healthy controls") |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    cu_nm,
    `Total` = ctot_nm,
    `Bound to factor B` = p_h[["bmax"]] * occ,
    `Unbound + non-specifically bound` = cu_nm / p_h[["fumax"]]
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-cu_nm, names_to = "component", values_to = "conc_nm")

ggplot(fig2, aes(cu_nm, conc_nm, colour = component, linetype = component)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.1, 1e4), ylim = c(10, 5e4)) +
  labs(
    x = "Unbound iptacopan (nM)",
    y = "Iptacopan (nM)",
    colour = NULL,
    linetype = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 2b of Burmeister Getz 2025 (model curves only)."
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

The factor B curve plateaus at fB,avail (1874 nM, about 790 ng/mL of
iptacopan-equivalent) while the non-specific line rises with slope
1 / fu,max = 4, reproducing the shape of Figure 2b.

## Figure 4 -- unbound iptacopan and factor B activity over a dosing profile

Figure 4 transforms the mean total-iptacopan profile of the healthy controls
(single 200 mg dose) into an unbound profile and a fractional factor B
activity (100% minus occupancy). The three curves were digitised by the
maintainers from the published figure at the times where each curve is
legible (the peak region is hidden by the legend). The total-iptacopan
readings drive the model; the unbound and activity readings are the targets.

```{r figure-4-data}
fig4 <- data.frame(
  time = c(6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 24, 36, 42, 48, 54, 60, 66, 72, 78, 84, 90),
  total = c(1773, 1425, 1178, 973, 849, 761, 670, 462, 418, 371, 296, 229, 181, 146, 115, 90.8, 72.3),
  unbound = c(253, 162, 90.8, NA, NA, 23.2, 14.0, NA, NA, 3.38, NA, NA, 1.20, 0.88, 0.70, 0.51, NA),
  activity = c(NA, 2.9, 4.8, 7.1, 12.1, 17.1, 22.3, 44.0, 49.8, 54.8, 61.8, 68.5, 75.7, 82.3, 85.1, 87.6, 90.5)
)

ev4 <- data.frame(
  id = 1L,
  time = fig4$time,
  evid = 0L,
  amt = 0,
  CP_IPTACOPAN_NGML = fig4$total
)
sim4 <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  readModelDb("BurmeisterGetz_2025_iptacopan_healthy"),
  events = ev4,
  keep = "CP_IPTACOPAN_NGML"
) |>
  as.data.frame()

fig4 <- fig4 |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    unbound_model = sim4$Cu,
    activity_model = 100 * (1 - sim4$occ),
    unbound_pct_diff = 100 * (unbound_model / unbound - 1),
    activity_diff = activity_model - activity
  )
```

```{r figure-4, fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 4.5}
fig4_long <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(time = fig4$time, value = fig4$total, series = "Total (digitised, model input)", source = "Published"),
  data.frame(time = fig4$time, value = fig4$unbound, series = "Unbound", source = "Published"),
  data.frame(time = fig4$time, value = fig4$unbound_model, series = "Unbound", source = "Model")
) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(value))

ggplot(fig4_long, aes(time, value, colour = series, shape = source, linetype = source)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +

  ) +

ggplot(fig4 |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(activity)), aes(time)) +
  geom_point(aes(y = activity, shape = "Published (digitised)"), size = 2) +
  geom_line(aes(y = activity_model, linetype = "Model")) +
  labs(
    x = "Nominal time after dosing (h)",
    y = "Fractional factor B activity (%)",

```

```{r figure-4-table}
fig4 |>
  dplyr::select(time, total, unbound, unbound_model, unbound_pct_diff, activity, activity_model, activity_diff) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Time (h)" = time,
    "Total (ng/mL)" = total,

stopifnot(
```

# Closed-form checks against the published numbers

The model is time-independent and has no dosing, so a PKNCA analysis has
nothing to act on; the checks below replace it. Each compares a model output
with a number printed in the paper.

## Mass balance

Rebuilding total iptacopan from the model's unbound concentration with the
forward binding equation (Figure 2a) must return the input.

```{r mass-balance}
# The solved output also carries bmax / kd / fumax, so the tabulated values
# are joined under distinct names.
mb <- sim |>
  dplyr::mutate(group = as.character(group)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    dplyr::rename(par_tab, p_bmax = bmax, p_kd = kd, p_fumax = fumax),
    by = "group"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    ctot_rebuilt = cu_nm + p_bmax * cu_nm / (p_kd + cu_nm) + cu_nm * (1 - p_fumax) / p_fumax,
    rel_err = abs(ctot_rebuilt / ctot_nm - 1)
  )
max(mb$rel_err)
stopifnot(max(mb$rel_err) < 1e-8)
```

## EC50 and EC90 (Table 3)

Table 3 gives, per group, the total iptacopan concentrations at which 50% and
90% of available factor B is occupied. Evaluating each model at those
concentrations should return occupancies of 0.50 and 0.90.

```{r ec-check}
ec_pub <- data.frame(
  group = group_levels,
  EC50 = c(412.04, 389.43, 306.28, 193.57),
  EC90 = c(857.43, 804.09, 622.24, 403.04)
)
ec_chk <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(ec_pub)), function(i) {
  s <- solve_group(models[[ec_pub$group[i]]], c(ec_pub$EC50[i], ec_pub$EC90[i]))
  data.frame(
    group = ec_pub$group[i],
    EC50 = ec_pub$EC50[i],
    occ_at_EC50 = s$occ[1],
    EC90 = ec_pub$EC90[i],
    occ_at_EC90 = s$occ[2]
  )
}))
ec_chk |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Group" = group,
    "EC50, Table 3 (ng/mL)" = EC50,
    "Model occupancy at EC50" = occ_at_EC50,
    "EC90, Table 3 (ng/mL)" = EC90,
    "Model occupancy at EC90" = occ_at_EC90
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4)
stopifnot(
  all(abs(ec_chk$occ_at_EC50 - 0.5) < 0.005),
  all(abs(ec_chk$occ_at_EC90 - 0.9) < 0.005)
)
```

## Distribution of drug at the healthy EC90

The paper states that at the healthy-control EC90 of 857.43 ng/mL, 83.1% of
iptacopan is bound to factor B, 12.6% to non-specific plasma proteins and 4.3%
is unbound.

```{r partition}
s90 <- solve_group(models[["Healthy controls"]], 857.43) |>
  dplyr::mutate(ctot_nm = CP_IPTACOPAN_NGML * 1000 / mw_iptacopan, cu_nm = Cu * 1000 / mw_iptacopan)
part <- data.frame(
  state = c("Bound to factor B", "Bound non-specifically", "Unbound"),
  published = c(83.1, 12.6, 4.3),
  model = 100 * c(
    p_h[["bmax"]] * s90$occ,
    s90$cu_nm * (1 - p_h[["fumax"]]) / p_h[["fumax"]],
    s90$cu_nm
  ) / s90$ctot_nm
)
part |>
  dplyr::rename("Binding state" = state, "Published (%)" = published, "Model (%)" = model) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
stopifnot(all(abs(part$model - part$published) < 0.5))
```

## Trough occupancy at 100 mg versus 200 mg twice daily

The paper reports that a 34% lower steady-state trough (100 mg vs 200 mg bid)
lowers end-of-interval factor B occupancy from 96% to 83% at average exposure,
and from 90% to 67% for exposures near the lower end of the population. The
model reproduces this self-consistently: invert the 200 mg occupancy to a
total trough, scale it by 0.66 and evaluate the 100 mg occupancy.

```{r trough}
total_at_occ <- function(occ, p) {
  cu <- occ * p[["kd"]] / (1 - occ)
  (cu / p[["fumax"]] + p[["bmax"]] * occ) * mw_iptacopan / 1000
}
trough <- data.frame(
  exposure = c("Average", "Lower end"),
  occ_200 = c(0.96, 0.90),
  occ_100_published = c(0.83, 0.67)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(trough_200 = sapply(occ_200, total_at_occ, p = p_h))
trough$occ_100_model <- solve_group(models[["Healthy controls"]], 0.66 * trough$trough_200)$occ
trough |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Exposure" = exposure,
    "Occupancy at 200 mg bid trough" = occ_200,
    "Implied 200 mg trough (ng/mL)" = trough_200,
    "Occupancy at 100 mg bid, published" = occ_100_published,
    "Occupancy at 100 mg bid, model" = occ_100_model
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
stopifnot(all(abs(trough$occ_100_model - trough$occ_100_published) < 0.025))
```

The published occupancies are rounded to whole percentages, which accounts for
the 1-2 point difference at average exposure.

## Unbound Cmax from total Cmax (Table 2)

Because the transform is monotone, each participant's unbound Cmax is the
model applied to their total Cmax. Applying the model to the geometric-mean
total Cmax gives an approximation to the geometric-mean unbound Cmax; it is
not exact, because the geometric mean of a nonlinear transform differs from
the transform of the geometric mean and because the binding parameters vary
between participants, which the group-level fit does not describe.

```{r cmax-u}
cmax <- data.frame(
  group = group_levels,
  cmax_total = c(3490, 3560, 3230, 3260), # Table 2 geometric means
  cmax_u_published = c(711, 905, 1070, 1450)
)
cmax$cmax_u_model <- sapply(seq_len(nrow(cmax)), function(i) {
  solve_group(models[[cmax$group[i]]], cmax$cmax_total[i])$Cu
})
cmax$pct_diff <- 100 * (cmax$cmax_u_model / cmax$cmax_u_published - 1)
cmax |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Group" = group,
    "Total Cmax, geo-mean (ng/mL)" = cmax_total,
    "Unbound Cmax, geo-mean, published (ng/mL)" = cmax_u_published,
    "Unbound Cmax, model (ng/mL)" = cmax_u_model,
    "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
stopifnot(all(abs(cmax$pct_diff) < 20))
```

Healthy controls, mild HI and severe HI agree within 5%. Moderate HI is 16%
low: that group's unbound Cmax varies much more between participants
(geometric CV 41.8%) than its total Cmax does (22.3%), which a single
group-level binding curve cannot reproduce.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Four files for four fits.** The paper fitted the binding model separately
  to each hepatic-function group (Results, 'Iptacopan PPB model'), so each
  group is its own model. Choose the file matching the population of
  interest; there is no covariate model linking the groups.
* **Total concentration is an input, not a PK model.** The paper publishes no
  structural iptacopan PK model. Supply `CP_IPTACOPAN_NGML` from observed
  concentrations or from an external iptacopan PK model.
* **Fitting direction.** The paper states the binding model was fitted to
  the total and unbound concentrations with `minpack.lm::nlsLM` and a
  proportional error model, but not which concentration was the response.
  The packaged model returns `Cu` from `Ctot` (eq. 2), the direction the paper
  uses for occupancy; the parameter values are the same either way.
* **Residual error.** The magnitude of the proportional error is not reported,
  so `propSd` is `fixed(0)`. The model gives deterministic predictions; it
  has no inter-individual variability because the source fit was a pooled
  per-group regression.
* **Observation name `Cu`.** The single output is the unbound concentration.
  It keeps the name `Cu` used across the library for unbound plasma
  concentration rather than `Cc`, which would imply total drug. The
  conventions checker flags a single-output `Cu` as non-canonical; this is
  expected here.
* **Units.** `bmax` and `kd` are in nM as tabulated; the model converts
  total and unbound iptacopan between ng/mL and nM with the molecular weight
  422.52 g/mol (Table 3 footnote b). The ug/mL figures for fB,avail in
  Table 3 assume a factor B molecular weight of 90 kDa. The Results text
  quotes 168.5 ug/mL for the healthy-control fB,avail, while Table 3 gives
  168.69 ug/mL (1874.30 nM); the model uses the nM value.
* **Rounded fu,max.** Table 3 gives fu,max to two decimals. Recomputing EC50
  and EC90 from the tabulated parameters reproduces Table 3 within 0.25%,
  which is the residual effect of that rounding.
* **Figure 4 digitisation.** The Figure 4 points were read from the published
  image by the maintainers; the peak region (about 1-5 h) is hidden by the
  figure legend and was not used.
